description: Given a list of accounts where each account is [name, email1, email2, ...], merge accounts that share at least one common email. Two accounts with the same name but no common emails remain separate. Return merged accounts with emails sorted.
examples:
Input: accounts = [["John","john@mail.com","john_newyork@mail.com"],["John","john@mail.com","john00@mail.com"],["Mary","mary@cool.com"],["John","johnnybravo@mail.com"]]
Output: [["John","john00@mail.com","john@mail.com","john_newyork@mail.com"],["Mary","mary@cool.com"],["John","johnnybravo@mail.com"]]
Explanation: The first two John accounts share "john@mail.com" and are merged. The third John has no shared emails.
intuition: Treat emails as nodes. Connect every email in an account to that account’s first email. Accounts sharing an email become one connected component. Run BFS to collect each component, sort its emails, and attach the owner’s name.
approach: Treat emails as nodes. Connect every email in an account to that account’s first email. Accounts sharing an email become one connected component. Run BFS to collect each component, sort its emails, and attach the owner’s name.
explanation:
1. Connect emails within each account in both directions. Using the first email as a hub is enough to connect the account.
2. Shared names alone do not connect accounts; shared emails do.
3. Each unvisited email starts a BFS for one merged account. Process one frontier at a time and mark neighbors before scheduling them.
4. Collect each distinct email once, sort the component, and prefix the owner’s name.
5. Keep accounts without shared email connections separate.
spaceComplexity: O(T + U) for the graph and traversal state

Mark a node when scheduling it so repeated paths cannot schedule it again.
Union-find with path compression speeds up repeated connectivity checks in the version below.

followUp.title: Union-find with path compression
followUp.label: Optimized
followUp.approach: Use Union-Find. Map each email to a parent email. For each account, union all emails in that account together. After processing, group emails by their root parent, attach the account name, sort emails, and return.
followUp.jsWalkthrough:
accounts = [
  ["John","john@mail.com","john_ny@mail.com"],
  ["John","john@mail.com","john00@mail.com"],
  ["Mary","mary@cool.com"]
]

Processing account 0 (John):
  firstEmail = "john@mail.com"
  i=1: email="john@mail.com" → parent={j@:j@}, union(j@,j@) → no-op
  i=2: email="john_ny@mail.com" → parent={j@:j@, jny@:jny@}
        union(j@, jny@) → parent[find(j@)=j@] = find(jny@)=jny@ → parent[j@]=jny@

Processing account 1 (John):
  firstEmail = "john@mail.com"
  i=1: email="john@mail.com" → already in parent
        union(j@, j@) → no-op
  i=2: email="john00@mail.com" → parent[j00@]=j00@
        union(j@, j00@) → find(j@)=jny@ → parent[jny@]=j00@

Processing account 2 (Mary):
  firstEmail = "mary@cool.com"
  parent[mary@]=mary@, union(mary@, mary@) → no-op

Grouping by root:
  find("john@mail.com") → follows chain to "john00@mail.com"
  find("john_ny@mail.com") → "john00@mail.com"
  find("john00@mail.com") → "john00@mail.com"
  Group "john00@mail.com" → all 3 John emails
  Group "mary@cool.com" → ["mary@cool.com"]

Result: [["John","john00@mail.com","john@mail.com","john_ny@mail.com"],["Mary","mary@cool.com"]]
followUp.explanation:
- parent maps each email to its parent in the Union-Find structure. email_to_name maps each email to the account name.
- For each account, initialize all emails in Union-Find and union them with the first email (connecting all emails in the same account).
- After processing all accounts, find the root of each email and group them.
- For each group, prepend the account name and sort the emails alphabetically.
- Union-Find automatically merges accounts that share emails across different account entries.
followUp.spaceComplexity: O(n) for the Union-Find structures and groupings

timeComplexityBreakdown.variables: T = total email occurrences in the input; U = unique emails. U ≤ T.

phases.label: Read email occurrences and initialize maps
Union each occurrence with its account’s first email
Find roots and group unique emails

simplifications: O(T + T log U + 2U log U + U)
O(T log U + U log U)
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: This conservative amortized bound uses log U for path compression without rank or size. Since U ≤ T, T log U also covers sorting. Email hashing and comparison are treated as constant time.

phases.label: Build the email graph and name map
Traverse all email components with BFS

simplifications: O(T) + O(T) + O(U log U) + O(U)
timeComplexityBreakdown.note: U ≤ T, so O(U + T) becomes O(T). All BFS traversals share visited. Sorting the separate groups costs at most O(U log U) in total. Email hashing and comparison are treated as constant time.
